question: In triangle ABC , BD perp AC at point D and angle DBC = 72^circ . There is a point E on BC such that angle CAE = 71^circ . What is the measure of angle AEB ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In right-angled ΔBDC, ∠C = 90° − ∠DBC = 90° − 72° = 18°.

In ΔAEC, side CE is extended to point B.

By the Exterior Angle Theorem, the exterior ∠AEB = ∠CAE + ∠C

⇒ ∠AEB = 71° + 18° = 89°.

**∴ The correct answer is 89°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ BD ⊥ AC at D, so ∠BDC = 90°.

⇒ ∠DBC = 72°.

⇒ E is a point on BC such that ∠CAE = 71°.

 
 
• 
•

 18° 
 71° 
 72° A B C D E 

**Calculation:**

⇒ In right-angled ΔBDC, the sum of angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠C = 180° − (∠BDC + ∠DBC)

⇒ ∠C = 180° − (90° + 72°) = 18°

⇒ In ΔAEC, the sum of interior angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠AEC = 180° − (∠CAE + ∠C)

⇒ ∠AEC = 180° − (71° + 18°) = 180° − 89° = 91°

⇒ Since B, E, and C lie on a straight line, ∠AEB and ∠AEC form a linear pair.

⇒ ∠AEB + ∠AEC = 180°

⇒ ∠AEB = 180° − 91° = 89°

**∴ The correct answer is 89°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is exactly equal to the sum of the measures of its two opposite (remote) interior angles. Using this theorem skips the need to find the third interior angle.

Angle Sum Property of a Triangle

The sum of all three interior angles of any planar triangle is always equal to 180°. It implies that if any two angles are known, the third can be found directly.

Linear Pair Axiom

When two angles form a straight continuous line, they are considered supplementary angles. This means their total sum will consistently measure exactly 180°.
